purpose: Teach: 下る/改める/件名/にせよ/借家/召集/所蔵/年頃

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業時、業績が、下る時、本気で、絶対、苦労したぞ、お父さん、覚えてる?お前にも、伝えたい、本気で、絶対、本当に、絶対、本気。
lines.en: When we started the company, there were times when things got really hard—do you remember, Dad? I want to pass that on to you. I mean it.
lines.style: Quiet, steady opening. Weight of years in the voice. Lean forward slightly on 'remember'—testing the continuity between generations. Let the trailing thought hang with gentle certainty, not wistfulness.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さんの代から、本気で、絶対、社是、改めるところがあれば、絶対、見直してまいります、本気で、感謝、本当に、絶対、本気。
lines.en: Yes. Since your time, I've made sure we review our company philosophy wherever it needs strengthening. I've inherited that commitment from you, and I'm grateful for it.
lines.style: Measured, respectful cadence. Not ceremonial—more intimate than that. Slight emphasis on 'inherited' as if placing something precious in both hands. Steady eye contact level throughout.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業時のメールの件名、本気で、私たち、絶対、こだわって、お得意様、本気で、絶対、ご好印象を、与えてきたぞ、絶対、本気、絶対。
lines.en: Back when we started, we were particular about everything—the subject lines in our emails, how we impressed our best clients. We took care with those things.
lines.style: Nostalgic but not distant. Voice thins slightly on 'took care with'—reaching back. Concrete, specific memory. End on a note of quiet pride, not regret.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。本気で、困難な、時代にせよ、絶対、当社、生き残れる、力、本気で、お父さんの代から、絶対、継承してきました、本気で、本当に、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. Even through difficult times, our company has survived because we inherited that strength from you. That's what kept us going.
lines.style: Calm affirmation. Light pause after 'difficult times' as if acknowledging weight but moving through it. Gratitude in the vocal texture, not the words alone. Steady, grounded tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業時の借家、本気で、お父さん、絶対、よく、覚えているぞ、お前にも、見せてやりたい、本気で、絶対、本当に、絶対、本気、絶対。
lines.en: The founding-era rental house—I remember it well. I wish I could show you what I see in it now, what it meant.
lines.style: Soft, almost vulnerable opening. The memory lives in his voice before the words. Slow pace. Let 'I wish I could show you' carry both longing and tenderness. Trail off as if sharing something kept close.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さんからの召集、本気で、絶対、いつでも、応じます、本気で、感謝、しております、本気で、本当に、絶対、本気、絶対、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. Whenever you call on me, I'll answer. I owe you everything for that.
lines.style: Simple, direct sincerity. No flourish. Weight on the second sentence—it's a vow, not a courtesy. Let the gratitude be earned, lived in, not performed.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業者の遺品、本気で、社内、絶対、所蔵、本当に、貴重な財産だ、お前にも、本気で、絶対、守って欲しい、本気で、絶対、頼んだぞ。
lines.en: The founder's belongings—we keep them in the office. They're precious to us. I want you to know I'll protect them for you.
lines.style: Firmer cadence, almost solemn. This is not a request—it's a charge being passed. Slight emphasis on 'protect.' Composed but emotionally present. The commitment is visible in how the voice holds.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さん、創業時、本気で、年頃の若さ、絶対、頑張ってきたんですよね、お母さんから、本気で、絶対、聞いております、本当に、感謝、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. When you started out, you were so young, and you worked so hard. Your mother told me all about it. I'm grateful for everything you built.
lines.style: Warm, wondering tone. The recognition of his father's youth carries genuine admiration. Slower pace on 'worked so hard'—each word is a small acknowledgment. Close on gratitude, not as duty but as discovery.
